children: Alpha Wave Ventures has offloaded Rs 550-crore worth shares in Pine Labs, the point of sale and payment systems provider, via open market transactions on September 2.

As per the block deals published on the stock exchanges, Alpha Wave Ventures II LP, the flagship global private equity fund managed by Alpha Wave Ventures GP, sold 3.54 crore shares, representing 3.07 percent of paid-up equity, in Pine Labs.
The above-mentioned shares worth Rs 549.92 crore were bought by nine domestic and global investors at a price of Rs 155.1 per share.
ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company emerged as the largest buyer amongst them, acquiring additional 1.03 crore shares (0.89 percent stake) in Pine Labs for Rs 160 crore.
Alpha Wave Ventures held 3.11 percent stake, and ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company has 1.25 percent shareholding in Pine Labs as of June 2026.

The remainder 2.51 crore equity shares (2.17 percent stake) worth Rs 390 crore in Pine Labs were acquired by Societe Generale, Edelweiss Mutual Fund, Goldman Sachs Investments Mauritius, Viridian Asia Opportunities Master Fund, Integrated Core Strategies (Asia), JM Financial MF, Morgan Stanley Asia Singapore, and Norges Bank on account of the Government Pension Fund Global.
Pine Labs shares rose 1.52 percent to Rs 162.32 amid volatility on the National Stock Exchange.

Meanwhile, CDPQ Infrastructures Asia III Inc, the subsidiary of global investment group CDPQ, has picked up 73.13 crore units (equivalent to 24 percent stake) in Brookfield-backed Altius Telecom Infrastructure Trust, the telecom towers InvIT, for Rs 12,067 crore.

On other side, Singapore’s sovereign wealth fund GIC-backed Anahera Investment sold 21.11 crore units (6.92 percent stake) for Rs 3,483.15 crore, and Brookfield-controlled BIF IV Jarvis India Pte offloaded 52.02 crore units (17.07 percent stake) for Rs 8,584.53 crore.
The above-mentioned 24 percent units exchanged at a price of Rs 165 per unit.

title: Alpha Wave Ventures offloads Rs 550-crore worth Pine Labs shares; ICICI Pru Life, Morgan Stanley among buyers
